title: The Kid on the Housetop
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A Kid climbed up on to the roof of an outhouse, attracted by the grass and other things that grew in the thatch; and as he stood there browsing away, he caught sight of a Wolf passing below, and jeered at him because he couldn't reach him. The Wolf only looked up and said, "I hear you, my young friend; but it is not you who mock me, but the roof on which you are standing."

questions.prompt: According to the passage, where does the Kid climb?
options: Onto a nearby wall
Up a tall tree
Up onto the roof of an outhouse
Onto a haystack in the yard

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what attracts the Kid to the roof?
options: The grass and other things growing in the thatch
The view of the surrounding fields
The shade it provides from the sun
A nest of birds he wanted to see

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Kid see while browsing on the roof?
options: A farmer walking by
Another kid climbing nearby
A flock of birds flying overhead
A Wolf passing below

questions.prompt: According to the passage, why does the Kid jeer at the Wolf?
options: Because the Wolf looked frightened
Because the Wolf couldn't reach him
Because the Wolf had tried to climb up earlier
Because the Wolf was chasing another animal

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Wolf say when he hears the Kid?
options: That he will remember the Kid's insult forever
That he is too tired to respond properly
That it is not the Kid who mocks him, but the roof he is standing on
That he will wait for the Kid to come down

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what point is the Wolf making about the source of the Kid's boldness?
options: The Kid's safety, not any real courage or advantage, is what allows him to mock the Wolf
The Kid genuinely believes he could defeat the Wolf in a fight
The roof itself is somehow insulting the Wolf on its own
The Wolf secretly agrees that the Kid is superior to him

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the Wolf remain calm rather than angry at being mocked?
options: He does not actually hear what the Kid is saying
He is too hungry to react to anything else
He believes the Kid will eventually come down and apologize
He recognizes that the Kid's taunt means nothing once he is no longer in a safe position

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "jeered" mean in "jeered at him"?
options: Warned or cautioned
Mocked or taunted
Waved or signaled
Questioned or interrogated

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "thatch" refer to in the passage?
options: A wooden fence around a yard
A type of tall grass in a field
Straw or plant material used to cover a roof
A small tool used for climbing

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable?
options: Courage that depends entirely on a safe position is not real courage at all
Wolves are always calm no matter how they are treated
Kids should never climb onto rooftops for any reason
Mocking someone is always harmless if you are out of reach

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what is the Kid doing while standing on the roof?
options: Watching for other wolves nearby
Calling out to other kids for help
Resting after a long climb
Browsing on the grass and plants there

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how does the Wolf address the Kid?
options: "Little fool"
"My young friend"
"Small creature"
"Foolish Kid"

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Wolf say he does hear from the Kid?
options: He hears nothing at all from him
He hears him but pretends not to
He hears him, meaning the taunt itself
He hears him singing rather than mocking

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what would likely happen if the Kid were on the ground instead of the roof?
options: He would probably not dare to mock the Wolf at all
He would mock the Wolf just as boldly as before
The Wolf would still ignore him completely
Nothing would change about the situation

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why might the Wolf's reply be considered a wise response rather than a defeat?
options: It proves the Wolf could climb the roof if he wanted to
It shows the Wolf plans to wait until nightfall to attack
It convinces the Kid to come down from the roof at once
It correctly identifies that the insult carries no real weight given the circumstances

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "mock" mean in "it is not you who mock me"?
options: To warn or alert
To make fun of or ridicule
To follow closely behind
To imitate exactly

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A Wolf climbs onto the roof to confront the Kid directly
A Kid is frightened into silence by the Wolf's reply
A Kid safely mocks a Wolf from a rooftop, and the Wolf points out that only his position, not real bravery, allows it
A Wolf chases the Kid off the roof successfully
